title: Students and opposition parties protest in Delhi against the CEC
seoTitle: Delhi protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

tea.why: Protesters allege the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls wrongly deleted large numbers of eligible voters.
tea.want: Resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and action over the alleged voter roll irregularities.
tea.changed: Oct 5: NSUI members were detained at a 'living dead' protest; INDIA bloc MPs plan a march to the EC on Oct 6.

summary: Student groups, the Aam Aadmi Party and other opposition groups have tried to gather at Delhi's Jantar Mantar since October 2 to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which they say removed eligible voters. Delhi Police refused permission and enforced prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS; 11 Metro stations were closed and mobile internet was suspended around the site on the first day. Protesters returned on each of the following days and were repeatedly detained and released, according to reports. Police registered three FIRs over the October 2 gathering and said some officers were bitten during the October 4 march; AISA alleged its national president was taken away in a private vehicle without a woman officer present, which police called baseless. On October 5 the NSUI held a symbolic 'living dead' protest. The INDIA bloc has announced a march by its MPs from Parliament to the Election Commission headquarters on October 6.
demands: Action on alleged deletions of voters in the SIR
response: Delhi Police denied permission, enforced Section 163 prohibitory orders and detained protesters who did not leave, registering three FIRs; police said some officers were bitten on Oct 4. The Election Commission's response is not reported in these sources.

crowd.text: hundreds gathered on roads around Jantar Mantar on Oct 2, Reuters reported

arrests.text: more than 1,000 detained on Oct 2 and over 150 on Oct 3, per Rediff; most were later released

updates.text: AAP leaders called on supporters to gather at Jantar Mantar on Gandhi Jayanti, Oct 2.
Police denied permission, shut 11 Metro stations and detained protesters and opposition leaders heading to Jantar Mantar.
Protesters returned; police said prohibitory orders stayed in force and registered three FIRs over the Oct 2 protest.
A citizens' march from India Gate was stopped; the AISA national president was detained and later released.
NSUI staged a 'living dead' protest near Jantar Mantar; several members were detained.
INDIA bloc announced a march by MPs from Parliament's Makar Dwar to the Election Commission on Oct 6.
